title: Tokenization Atlas
intro: Who is putting real-world assets onchain, the platforms and ledgers they use, and where those tokens are custodied, priced and traded.
initiativesHeading: How the world’s largest companies are tokenizing assets

layers.name: Asset issuers & managers
layers.description: The firms whose assets go on-chain: fund managers tokenizing treasuries and money market funds, private credit and private markets funds, banks issuing deposit tokens, and issuers of tokenized commodities and stocks. They decide the legal wrapper and who may hold the token.
watch: Tokenized AUM by product and month-on-month growth
Legal structure: fund share class, SPV, or direct registration
Eligibility: qualified purchasers only, or retail access
Use of tokens as collateral and in DeFi

layers.name: Tokenization platforms
layers.description: The issuance layer: platforms and digital transfer agents that structure the token, handle investor onboarding and the register, and enforce transfer rules on-chain. Most asset managers rent this layer rather than build it.
watch: Transfer-agent and broker-dealer licences
Token standards for permissioned transfers (ERC-3643, ERC-1400)
Multi-chain issuance and cross-chain transfer
Secondary trading and redemption mechanics

layers.name: Chains & ledgers
layers.description: Where tokenized assets live. Public chains hold most tokenized value; permissioned and institutional networks focus on privacy, settlement finality and bank participation.
watch: Share of tokenized RWA value per chain
Privacy and permissioning for institutions
Interoperability between public and private networks
Settlement in tokenized cash or stablecoins

layers.name: Custody, data & market infra
layers.description: The plumbing that makes tokenized assets usable by institutions: custodians, oracles that publish NAV and reserves, interoperability, and incumbent market infrastructure such as CSDs and DTCC moving on-chain.
watch: Qualified custody for tokenized securities
NAV, proof-of-reserve and corporate-action data on-chain
Cross-chain messaging for regulated assets
Incumbent CSDs and DTCC tokenization services

layers.name: Distribution & markets
layers.description: Where investors actually buy, trade or use tokenized assets: brokers and apps offering tokenized stocks, exchanges and ATSs, and DeFi venues that accept tokenized treasuries as collateral.
watch: Retail access to tokenized stocks by region
24/7 trading and settlement with stablecoins
Tokenized treasuries accepted as collateral
On/off-ramps and stablecoin settlement for tokenized products

layers.name: Regulation
layers.description: Regimes that decide whether a tokenized asset is a security, who may issue and trade it, and how records of ownership are recognised. Sandboxes and pilots are moving into permanent rules.
watch: SEC treatment of tokenized securities and exemptions
EU DLT Pilot Regime review and expansion
UK Digital Securities Sandbox progress
Asian frameworks: MAS Project Guardian, Hong Kong Ensemble
